essence: What never stood cannot stand another: consciousness fits itself to this and I, orders inert selves by double certainty, and completes severed grasping in self-rest (vv10-15).
The same self twofold — breath-bound atom, unbroken whole — gathers in one continuous end-ground where nothing shows more inert than shining (vv16-18).

sections.SUMMARY: What never stood cannot stand another: unwon herself, grasp-less awareness grounds no other being. Consciousness fits to ground another's showing by saying this — and again, itself, by saying I. By exclusion and inclusion both, certainty orders inert selves: fixed order, ground, winning, winding-up. Near-unreal in self, inert ones are shining's own; shining alone is, through selves own and other. No experience stands apart from distinct-and-indistinct assurance, apart from linked ungrasping shining. Cut-off this-grasping completes in self-rest: I-am-this is this. One self twofold — breath-bound atom, unbroken whole. Both gather in one end-ground through linking alone. At the limit, in no-parting I-knowing, nothing shows more inert than shining.
sections.FUNCTION: Builds the positive account after the demolition: self-grounding first, then the two sayings, certainty's offices, borrowed being, grasp as experience, completion in rest, the twofold one, the gathering, the seal.
sections.KEY TERMS: pratiṣṭhāspadatā (standing-placehood) · idam/aham (this/I) · vyatireka/itara (exclusion/inclusion) · asatkalpa (near-unreal) · anusaṃdhāna (linking) · paryantabhūmi (end-ground) · ahaṃvid (I-knowing) · vimarśa kept as grasping (see p01 NOTE)
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Passage 2 of 3: vv. 10–18. The knower must first ground itself. Vṛ read as Utpaladeva's own (authorship open — see p01 NOTE).
sections.EXPLANATION: Self-grounding preconditions all grounding; two sayings, two poles; certainty's four offices with double concomitance; inert being as borrowed shining with autonomy dawning inside; experience identified with grasping; severed grasping completed in rest; one self shown twofold; gathered by linking; sealed at the limit.
sections.BOUNDARY: Feminine subject kept (she). itara read as anvaya side with the Vṛ. No live token forks in this passage.
sections.RELATED: Īśvarapratyabhijñā ābhāsa/vimarśa · Ratié 2007 otherness/ūha backs v17 · Spanda linking · Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya rest · Lawrence 2009 · Mundra & Godbole 2022

rasa.sthayibhava: śama (settling) as self-rest completing severed grasping
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is rest itself (viśrānti, kṛtārthatā): the passage lands twice in settling — grasping completed (v15), both measures gathered (v17). The vyabhicāri is wonder at the twofold one (v16): atom and unbroken, same self. Abhinava's śānta as the relish of recognition completed — homecoming after demolition.
